subject: physics_2
question_text: State the expression for the reactance of (i) an inductor and (ii) a capacitor.

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: inductive reactance XL = ωL and capacitive reactance XC = 1/ωC; unit check: ωL is s⁻¹ × H = Ω and 1/(ωC) is 1/(s⁻¹ × F) = Ω. Capital-letter subscripts (X with subscript L) have no Unicode form, so the symbols are written XL and XC with their full names on first use.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Inductive reactance
lines: For an inductor of inductance L on an a.c.
supply of angular frequency ω, the inductive
XL rises when the frequency rises.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the symbol and give the expression.
steps.why: Reactance is the opposition an inductor offers to a.c. — it grows with both L and ω, so XL = ωL is the whole behaviour: more inductance or a faster supply, more opposition.
common_mistakes: Writing XL = L/ω or XL = 1/ωL. The inductive reactance is the product ωL.
Leaving out the unit. XL is measured in ohm (Ω), like a resistance.

recall.must_convey: That the inductive reactance is XL = ωL, and it increases with frequency.

steps.memory_tip: L multiplies, C divides: XL = ωL and XC = 1/ωC.

steps.label: Capacitive reactance
lines: For a capacitor of capacitance C, the
XC falls when the frequency rises.
Both reactances are measured in ohm (Ω).
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The reciprocal form, and the unit ohm written once for both.
steps.why: The capacitor's opposition is the reciprocal — a larger C or a faster supply moves more charge each cycle, so the opposition 1/ωC falls. The two formulas together answer the question.
common_mistakes: Writing XC = ωC. The capacitive reactance is the reciprocal, 1/ωC.
Swapping the two: XL = 1/ωC and XC = ωL is the classic exchange.

recall.must_convey: That the capacitive reactance is XC = 1/ωC, it decreases with frequency, and both reactances are in ohm.

steps.memory_tip: At high frequency the inductor blocks (ωL large) and the capacitor passes (1/ωC small).

insider_note: Write both expressions with their names — inductive reactance XL, capacitive reactance XC — and give the unit ohm once.
